transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-18 15:00 UTC, Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Maya Chen, Luis Ortega, Ravi Patel (Redwood) / Priya Raman, Tom Hsu, Ellen Park, Nico Alvarez (Alder)

Summary: quick status on the on‑prem pilot, review of canary kernel upgrade, routing fallback checks, and security notes. Agreed next steps and owners.

Topics: kernel upgrade canary; KV cache behavior under 8-bit quant; VPC egress and NAT pathing; audit logs & KMS; runbook handoff to NetOps.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: okay hi everyone, thanks for joining — we'll kick off, um, quick agenda — status, canary plan, netops runbook, then action items. Priya you want to start with any blockers?
[00:18] Priya: yeah hi. main thing this week — we saw two spikes in tail latency during mid‑day traffic, looks like coupling between batching increases and a routing path switch. not sure if it's KV cache miss storms or the fallback routing firing.
[00:33] Luis: got it. on our side we instrumented the KV cache metrics, there were several prefix misses aligned with the spike. we suspect sequence length distribution changed after yesterday's rollout of a new prompt template, so batch sizes got bigger.
[00:48] Tom: to add, netops toggled a new egress trunk on friday, the kenary — the canary — sorry — the canary nodes were moved through a new firewall set. could be asymmetric routing.
[01:02] Nico: yep that was me, we enabled a secondary egress to test throughput. i can share traceroutes, but initial look shows some flows take longer MTU path.
[01:12] Maya: cool, let's capture that as a hypothesis: batch size bump + asymmetric egress + KV miss. Luis, did quantization changes factor in? you ran the 8‑bit profile earlier right?
[01:26] Luis: i ran it in the lab cluster — 8‑bit quant gives us a 28% token cost reduction and median latency improvement but tail is sensitive when KV cache misses occur; reconstructing K V cash is slightly heavier with current kernel.
[01:40] Priya: that matches what we saw — median fine, tails bad. is there a quick mitigation we can do while you patch the kernel?
[01:50] Luis: two immediate levers — reduce max batch size for that route and enable prefix caching for common prompts, and then fallback to non‑quant path for requests exceeding N tokens. but that introduces cost impact.
[02:05] Ellen: from security perspective we need to document the fallback decision tree; also SOC 2 requirements on audit logs: how do rollbacks appear in logs and who triggers them.
[02:14] Maya: yes we have a template for an audit play; we'll share the SOC 2 summary and how KMS/HSM integrates with Redwood Private. Ellen, is there a preferred KMS vendor?
[02:23] Ellen: we use an internal HSM with a KMIP front end, but the requirement is that Redwood can integrate via standard KMS APIs and that key rotation events are logged.
[02:33] Ravi: noted — Redwood's private control plane supports KMS abstraction, we can create a mapping doc. i'll own the runbook handoff with Nico.
[02:41] Nico: good. can you include the firewall rules excerpt? we need to know exact egress IPs for canary and kenary nodes.
[02:50] Maya: yes we'll include IP list and a recommended NAT configuration for the VPC.
[02:55] Tom: also we saw a small packet fragmentation issue — MTU mismatch — during the spike. might be making tails worse.
[03:03] Luis: MTU plus extra TLS renegotiation on the new path — that combo is bad. our patch reduces TCP re‑handshake by keeping sockets warm, but it requires the kernel upgrade.
[03:16] Priya: timeline? we need staging canary next week ideally.
[03:20] Maya: proposed timeline: canary start 2026‑11‑23, two days of low‑traffic validation, then widen on 2026‑11‑25 if no regressions. we'll push patch notes today.
[03:31] Priya: okay, and what about rollback if tail latency worsens?
[03:36] Luis: automatic circuit breaker — if P95 increases by > 40% for 5 minutes, routing policy will fallback to the previous kernel variant and also switch to the non‑quant path for that route. that gets us safety.
[03:49] Ellen: can you make sure the fallback events generate an audit record with user context and ticket link?
[03:55] Luis: yes, that will be part of the rollback hook.
[04:00] Maya: quick note on costs: fallback to non‑quant will raise token spend ~x1.4. we flagged this in the cost dashboard; we'll send a tokenized cost estimate for the pilot window.
[04:12] Priya: good. on observability, can you give us a CSV of latency per sequence length? that's what our model team wants.
[04:20] Luis: yes, i'll run a 1k request sweep and attach the CSV. expecting to have it by sunday.
[04:27] Tom: also, are there any changes required to our side for TLS ciphers or is default fine?
[04:33] Maya: default should be fine but we'll list recommended ciphers and minimum TLS version in the runbook.
[04:38] Nico: about NAT and IPs — do you support ephemeral source IPs from the canary? we prefer static so ACLs are easier.
[04:45] Maya: we can provide static egress IP ranges for the canary nodes; we'll include the CIDR block in the doc.
[04:50] Priya: one other item — model version pinning. during the canary we want to pin the exact model hash so we can compare outputs pre/post kernel. how do we capture that?
[05:00] Luis: you can pin via the deployment config; we will also record model hash in traces so you can diff outputs. we'll add a prompt set to run for regression checks.
[05:09] Ravi: i'll coordinate the canary test harness with Priya, include the prompt set.
[05:14] Maya: perfect. anything else on security or procurement?
[05:17] Ellen: procurement just needs the updated SLA language that covers canary/rollback windows. i'll send a redline after this call.
[05:24] Maya: great. to recap — action owners: maya send SOC2 + KMS checklist; luis run latency sweep and 8bit quant csv; nico provide traceroutes and confirm NAT static IP; priya provide prompt traces. canary target 11/23.
[05:40] Tom: quick clarifying question — the routing policy that triggers fallback, is that per‑customer route or global?
[05:46] Luis: per‑route. we scope by endpoint path and model variant. so you can have one route on quant and another on non‑quant.
[05:56] Priya: that helps. thanks.
[05:59] Maya: last thing — we'll also share a short video walkthrough of the runbook and a one‑page cheat sheet for NetOps.
[06:07] Nico: that'd be super helpful.
[06:10] Maya: awesome, we'll follow up with links. meeting adjourned, thanks everyone.

End recap + explicit next steps repeated at the end: share patch notes (link), runbook draft (link), latency CSV (link).
